claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
A hierarchical microstructure with grain sizes between 2 and 5 μm and a bimodal grain distribution will increase strength.
A hierarchical microstructure with grain sizes between 2 and 5 μm and a bimodal grain distribution will increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
The hierarchical grain structure enhances strain hardening.
The hierarchical grain structure reduces microcracking.
A bimodal grain distribution combines the strength benefit of fine grains with the ductility benefit of coarse grains.
The intervention will raise yield strength from 800 MPa to 960 MPa, a 20% increase over the unmodified baseline.
The intervention will raise tensile ductility from 10% to 13%, a 30% relative increase over the unmodified baseline.
The predicted properties are comparable to or exceed state-of-the-art values for eutectic high-entropy alloys.
A fine-to-coarse grain ratio between 1:1 and 1:3 optimizes the strength-ductility balance.
The optimal grain size and grain distribution may depend on alloy composition.
The optimal grain size and grain distribution may depend on processing conditions.
Prior research supports the proposed grain-size effects in high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improvements of 20% in yield strength and 30% in ductility, but the falsification rule only requires improvements exceeding 18% and 22%. Thus, results below the stated predictions could nevertheless avoid falsification.
